properties.program:
# Animation tab: frames 50, play-mode loop
# inputs: lam (wavelength), amp (amplitude)
view 0, -45, 120, 45
k = 2 * pi / lam
w = 2 * pi * t

# the water, filled strip by strip: one thin four-cornered poly per
# unit of x, stroked in its own colour so the seams do not show
repeat 120
  y0 = amp * sin(k * i - w)
  y1 = amp * sin(k * (i + 1) - w)
  poly i, -45, i, y0, i + 1, y1, i + 1, -45  with color "#4682b4", fill "#4682b4", width 0
end

# the still-water level
line 0, 0, 120, 0  with color "#b0c4de", width 0.4, dash "dash"

# one wavelength, crest to crest, riding along with the wave
c = lam * (0.25 + t - floor(0.25 + t))
dimension c, amp + 5, c + lam, amp + 5  with width 0.5

# a cork at x = 60: the wave runs past it, the cork only bobs
circle 60, amp * sin(k * 60 - w), 3  with fill "orange"

text 60, -40, "wavelength %.0f    amplitude %.0f", lam, amp  with font 4, color "white"

properties.text: THE TRAVELLING WAVE -- a Figure node that animates on its own and fills an area.  The Animation tab gives it 50 frames played in a loop at 25 fps, and the program shifts the wave by one wavelength over the film with the built-in variable t, so the loop is seamless.  The water is FILLED strip by strip: a repeat loop draws one thin four-cornered poly per unit of x, stroked in its own colour so the seams do not show -- the way to fill under any curve.  Spin the wheel over the knobs while it runs: WAVELENGTH sets the crest-to-crest distance (the bar above the water rides along with a crest), AMPLITUDE the height.  Watch the orange cork: the wave runs past it, but the cork only bobs up and down -- the water does not travel with the wave.  Open the Figure (double-click) to see the program.
